title: Negative questions; echo questions; questions with that-clauses
subtitle: Didn't she realise? / He's what?
summary: Use negative questions to suggest, persuade or criticise, use echo questions to check what you heard, and know when that must be left out.

lesson.heading: Negative questions
lesson.text: We usually make a negative yes/no or wh-question with an auxiliary verb (*have, did, would* ...) + **-n't**. We use them to suggest, to persuade, to criticise and so on.

examples.text: **Wouldn't** it be better to go tomorrow?
**Why don't** we go out for a meal?
*A:* Can you lend me £10? *B:* Again? **Haven't** you got any money left?

lesson.heading: not after the subject: more emphatic
lesson.text: In formal contexts, or when we want to give the negative special emphasis - to show that we are angry or very surprised, or to persuade someone strongly - we put **not** after the subject. This happens particularly in yes/no questions rather than wh-questions.

examples.text: **Did she not realise** that she'd broken it?
examples.note: less emphatically Didn't she realise that ...?

examples.text: **Can you not** get there a bit earlier?

left.label: More emphatic: never, no, nobody, nothing, nowhere
examples: Have you **nowhere** to go? (or Do you have nowhere to go?)

right.label: Less emphatic or more informal: -n't + ever / any / anybody
examples: **Haven't** you got **anywhere** to go? (or Don't you have anywhere ... ?)

lesson.heading: Suggestions and criticism with why
lesson.text: Make a suggestion with **Why not + verb** or **Why don't / doesn't ...** - but never *Why do not ...*. **Why didn't ...** is not used for a suggestion; depending on intonation and context it can criticise someone.

examples.text: **Why didn't** you tell me that in the first place?

lesson.heading: Exclamations
lesson.text: Negative question forms, usually said with a **falling** intonation, are used in exclamations that give an opinion.

lesson.heading: Echo questions
lesson.text: Echo questions check something we didn't hear properly or found surprising. We can repeat the whole sentence with a **rising** intonation, or focus on one part with a stressed wh-word or a phrase with *how*. **what** or *do* + **what** focuses on the verb.

examples.text: *A:* Tala's lost her job. *B:* **Tala's lost her job?**
*A:* Leon's arriving at 6:30. *B:* **When's Leon arriving?** / **Leon's arriving when?**
*A:* We paid £3,000 for the painting. *B:* **How much did you pay?** / **You paid how much?**
*A:* We paid £3,000 for the painting. *B:* **You what?** / **You did what?**
*A:* I think she's having a sleep. *B:* **She's what?** / **She's doing what?**

lesson.heading: Questions with that-clauses
lesson.text: A wh-question can refer to a following **that**-clause, particularly after *expect, hope, reckon, say, suggest, suppose* and *think*, and *that* can be left out. But when the wh-word is the **subject, object or complement** of the verb in that clause, we do **not** use *that*.

examples.text: **When do you reckon (that)** you'll finish the job?
**What did you think was** in the box?
examples.wrong: What did you think that was in the box

examples.text: **Who do you expect will** read your blog?
examples.wrong: Who do you expect that will read your blog

lesson.text: Why don't you ... ? offers help; Why didn't you ... ? usually complains. Choose the tense carefully.

exercises.prompt: *A:* Can you lend me £10? *B:* Again? ___ any money left?
exercises.explanation: A negative question with -n't expressing surprise or mild criticism.

exercises.prompt: *A:* I've had to bring the children with me. *B:* Why? ___ a babysitter?
exercises.explanation: The past form of can in a negative question: Couldn't you ... ?

exercises.prompt: *A:* I've put my bike in the sitting room. *B:* The sitting room! ___ it outside?
exercises.explanation: A negative question used to persuade someone to do something else.

exercises.prompt: Match each -n't question with its more emphatic equivalent using never, no, nobody or nowhere.

pairs.left: Haven't you any interest in maths at all?
pairs.right: Have you no interest in maths at all?

pairs.left: Couldn't you find anywhere else to sleep?
pairs.right: Could you find nowhere else to sleep?

pairs.left: Can't you remember anything about the accident?
pairs.right: Can you remember nothing about the accident?

pairs.left: Why don't I ever do well in exams?
pairs.right: Why do I never do well in exams?

pairs.left: Isn't there anybody you can ask for help?
pairs.right: Is there nobody you can ask for help?

exercises.prompt: *A:* I'm annoyed that you didn't come to the meeting. *B:* Why? ___ my email saying I'd be on holiday?
exercises.explanation: A negative question defending yourself against a criticism.

exercises.prompt: *A:* He's leaving at the end of next week. *B:* He's leaving ___?
exercises.explanation: An echo question can put a stressed wh-word where the information was.

exercises.prompt: *A:* It will cost about £15,000. *B:* It'll cost ___?
exercises.explanation: Amounts are echoed with how much: It'll cost how much? or It'll what?

exercises.statement: How do you think that Twitter will have changed our lives in ten years' time?
exercises.explanation: Correct. how is not the subject, object or complement of the that-clause, so that can stay.

exercises.prompt: You have only just found out that your friend changed her number. Which question is right?
options: Why didn't you tell me you'd changed your number?
Why did not you tell me you'd changed your number?
Why not you told me you'd changed your number?
exercises.explanation: In this kind of question we use the contracted didn't; Why did not you ... ? is not used.

exercises.statement: *A:* Mariam isn't answering her phone. *B:* Why do you not email her?
exercises.explanation: Why don't you email her? A suggestion uses Why not + verb or Why don't ... , never Why do not ...

exercises.statement: Who do you expect that will read your blog?
exercises.explanation: Who do you expect will read your blog? When the wh-word is the subject of the following clause, we leave out that.

exercises.prompt: You are astonished that she broke it without noticing. Make an emphatic negative question.
exercises.answer: Did she not realise that she'd broken it?
exercises.explanation: not after the subject is more emphatic than Didn't she realise ... ?
